`lamb_run()` accepts files as people actually save them. To do that it has to
make decisions about the file: which column holds the gene names, whether the
table is turned round, whether the numbers are counts or already on a log
scale. This page lists every one of those decisions.

Three principles apply throughout:

1. **Standard libraries where a standard exists.** Excel is read with `readxl`,
   HDF5 (`.h5`, `.h5ad`) with `rhdf5` or `hdf5r`, parquet with `arrow`, sparse
   matrices with `Matrix`, PAM50 with `genefu`, scores with `singscore`.
2. **Where no standard exists, the rule is written here, and most rules say so
   in the run log (`technical/run_log.txt`) when they fire.**
3. **When a file is ambiguous, LAMB stops and says why** rather than guessing.
   Where a guess could be wrong and cannot be checked from the data, an
   argument lets you state the answer instead.

## Why scaling rarely changes a call

LAMB scores each sample by ranking its genes against each other (singscore).
Any transformation that keeps the order of genes inside a sample, such as
taking logs or z-scoring a sample, leaves every call unchanged. Only three
things can change calls:

- **Normalising counts by gene length** (counts to TPM), which reorders genes.
- **Centring each gene across samples**, which reorders genes inside a sample.
- **Values becoming missing.**

The rules below are built around those three.

## Bulk tables

| Situation | Rule | Run log says |
|---|---|---|
| Separator | Chosen from the first lines: tab, `;`, `,` or whitespace. | "Read … with ';' as separator" (when not tab or comma) |
| Decimal comma | Assumed when the separator is not a comma and numbers use `,` as the decimal mark. | "… and decimal comma" |
| Thousands separators | `1,234.5`, `1.234,5`, `1 234` and `1'234` are read as one number. | – |
| Byte-order mark, leading `#` comment lines, blank lines | Skipped. | – |
| Header one field short (R `write.table`), blank top-left cell | Accepted: the first column holds row names. | – |
| No header row | Only for two-column files (one sample, named after the file) and HTSeq / STAR outputs. Otherwise LAMB stops: sample names would be unknown. | "No header row: one sample, named after the file" |
| Which column holds gene names | The text column where the largest share of values are known HGNC symbols (at least 25%, preferred at 50% or more), else Ensembl gene IDs (at least 25%). Symbols win a tie. | "Gene names taken from column '…'" |
| Most gene names unrecognised | Fewer than half the rows are human gene symbols or Ensembl IDs that map, and fewer than 1,000 reference-universe genes are present. LAMB stops and shows examples. | the stop message |
| No such column | If the column *headers* look like genes, the table is turned round (below). Otherwise LAMB stops: probe IDs or other identifiers must be converted to symbols first. | the stop message |
| Turned-round table (samples in rows) | Transposed when the column headers, not a column of values, look like genes (same 25% rule). | "the table was turned round (transposed)" |
| Gene names not in upper case (`Gata3`) | LAMB stops: these are mouse-style names, and LAMB is built for human tumours. Human names in lower case must be converted to upper case first. | the stop message |
| Other text columns (descriptions, a second ID column) | Dropped. | named in the log |
| Numeric annotation columns | Dropped when named Entrez ID, length, effective length, chromosome, start, end, strand, GC content or width (any common spelling). | "Ignored annotation column(s) …: GeneLength" |
| Text in a numeric column (`#N/A`, `-`, `null`, `NaN`) | Read as missing, when at least 90% of the column is numbers. | "… cell(s) held text where a number was expected" |
| Summary rows (`Total`, `Sum`, `__no_feature`, STAR's `N_unmapped` …) | Dropped. | "Dropped summary row(s) …" |
| Gene names that look like dates (`1-Mar`, `9-Sep`) | Kept, with a warning: Excel converted them, and they will not match. | "gene name(s) look like dates" |
| Repeated sample names | A suffix is added (`S1`, `S1_1`). | "Some sample names were repeated" |
| Sample column with no name | Named after its position. | named in the log |
| GEO series matrix as downloaded | LAMB stops: it holds probe IDs and description lines. Map probes to symbols with the platform (GPL) annotation first. | the stop message |
| Fewer than 1,000 genes | Run, with a warning: probably not a whole-transcriptome file. | "Warning: only … genes" |
| A single-cell count matrix saved as a text table (500 or more columns, over 70% zeros, whole numbers) | LAMB stops: it scores groups of cells, not single cells. Give a 10x folder, an `.h5ad` or an `.rds` object, with clusters. | the stop message |
| All values missing, all zero, or all negative | LAMB stops. | the stop message |

## Quantifier files and folders

Recognised by their column headers, never by column position:

| File | Column used | Units |
|---|---|---|
| Salmon `quant.sf` | `TPM` | TPM |
| kallisto `abundance.tsv` | `tpm` | TPM |
| RSEM `genes.results` / `isoforms.results` | `TPM` (isoforms summed by `gene_id`) | TPM |
| featureCounts | the count columns (Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length ignored) | counts |
| STAR `ReadsPerGene.out.tab` | the strand column with the most counts | counts |
| HTSeq-count | the count column (`__` rows dropped) | counts |

Per-transcript files are summed to genes only when the transcript names carry
the gene (GENCODE `ENST…|ENSG…|…|SYMBOL|` format). Otherwise LAMB stops and
asks for a gene-level file or a tx2gene table: guessing the gene of a
transcript ID is not safe.

A **folder** of per-patient files is combined on the genes every file shares.
Mixed formats or mixed units in one folder are refused. When fewer than half of
the genes are shared, the log warns that the files may use different
annotations.

## What the numbers are

| Values | Detected when | What is done |
|---|---|---|
| Raw counts | all whole numbers, none negative, largest above 100, and not summing to about one million per sample; or a counts format (featureCounts, STAR, HTSeq) | counts to TPM with the bundled gene lengths, then log2(TPM + 1) |
| Rounded TPM | all whole numbers, and every sample sums to between 500,000 and 1,010,000 with sample totals within 2% of each other | log2(x + 1) |
| TPM / FPKM | a TPM format; or largest value above 100, none negative, not all whole numbers | log2(x + 1) |
| Already log | largest value 100 or less; or any negative value | used as they are |
| **Centred per gene** | 3 or more samples, some values negative, and over 80% of genes have a mean or a median of 0 across samples |

**Whole numbers that are not counts** (rounded intensities, or rounded TPM
for a subset of genes that no longer sums to one million) look like counts and
are read as counts. When you know what the numbers are, say
so:

```r
lamb_run("table.csv", values = "tpm")   # or "counts", "log2"
```

## Duplicates

| Duplicate | Rule |
|---|---|
| Gene names, counts | Summed. |
| Gene names, other values | The row with the highest mean is kept. |
| Gene symbols in single-cell / spatial data | Summed (they are counts). |
| Sample names | A suffix is added. |
| `LAMBclassifier()` called directly on a matrix | The first occurrence is scored, with a warning. |

## Missing values

Missing values are never replaced by zero or by an average. A missing value is
treated exactly like a gene the platform did not measure, but for that sample
only:

- **A sample without missing values** is scored exactly as it always was.
- **A sample with missing values** is ranked and scored on its own measured
  genes. Each signature still needs at least 3 of its genes; below that it
  cannot be scored, the decision step that needs it cannot be evaluated, and
  the sample is **not classifiable**.
- **Fewer than 60% of a signature's genes** (after that sample's gaps) flags
  the call as resting on few genes, as on a targeted panel.
- **A gap outside the signatures** only removes that gene from the ranking,
  so scores move very slightly (by about one rank step).
- **A whole sample missing** is not classifiable; the others are unaffected.

The note in `LAMB_calls.csv` says how many signature values were missing and
whether the sample was scored on its measured genes or could not be classified.
Zeros are not missing values: a 0 is scored as a silent gene. Store "not
measured" as empty or `NA`.

## Single-cell and spatial data

| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| Platform | Recognised from the files present (for example `experiment.xenium`, `spatial/tissue_positions.csv`, `*_exprMat_file.csv`, `cell_by_gene.csv`), never from folder names. |
| Spatial files as downloaded | Visium: a folder holding `spatial/` and the matrix, also when the matrix keeps its download name (`<sample>_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5`); the matrix `.h5` or `filtered_feature_bc_matrix/` given on its own is read with the `spatial/` beside it. Visium HD: the `square_008um` bins; when only other bin sizes are present, the finest one above 2 um, and the run log says which. A single bin folder, or its matrix, reads that bin. CosMx and MERSCOPE: one run per folder, its files matched by their shared prefix (`<run>_exprMat_file.csv` with `<run>_metadata_file.csv`, `<run>cell_by_gene.csv` with `<run>cell_metadata.csv`); with several runs in a folder, give one run's expression file. |
| Matrix Market files under other names | A folder holding exactly one `.mtx`, one `*genes.tsv` or `*features.tsv`, and one `*barcodes.tsv` (as GEO atlases publish them) is read like a 10x folder. A one-column gene file is taken as symbols. |
| Counts | Raw counts are required. In `.h5ad`, the first whole-number matrix among `layers/counts`, `raw/X`, `X` is used; if none is whole numbers, LAMB stops (log-normalised values cannot be summed into pseudobulk). |
| Groups of cells | The instrument's or object's clusters: 10x / Xenium / Visium graph-based clusters, Seurat active identities, SingleCellExperiment `colLabels()`, an `.h5ad` obs column named `leiden`, `louvain`, `cluster(s)` or `seurat_clusters`. Otherwise name any cell annotation column, `clusters = "cell_type"` (an `.h5ad` obs column, Seurat `meta.data`, SingleCellExperiment `colData`, or a `metadata.csv` next to a matrix whose first column is the cell barcode); columns with 2 to 500 distinct values, and at most one per ten cells, are offered, and the message lists them. Or give a file, `clusters = "my_clusters.csv"` (cell id, cluster). CosMx and MERSCOPE have no clusters of their own. |
| Pseudobulk | Counts summed per cluster, then log2(CPM + 1). |
| Small clusters | Under 50 cells (`min_cells`): listed, not classified. |
| Cell-type gate | In each cluster's pseudobulk, genes are ranked and each module (epithelial, immune, vascular, adipocyte, fibroblast) is scored as the mean percentile rank of its 3 highest-ranked genes; a module needs 3 measured genes. A cluster is classified unless another module ranks above the epithelial one; such clusters read "Not epithelial", named by what dominates, and their scores stay in `technical/`. With fewer than 3 epithelial module genes on the panel, every cluster is classified. `tumour_clusters =` classifies named clusters whatever their markers. |
| Epithelial_share | The share of cells detecting at least one of EPCAM, CDH1, KRT5/7/8/14/17/18/19, CLDN4/7, ELF3, GRHL2, ESRP1, ERBB3, SPINT2 (those on the panel; empty when none is). Reported in `LAMB_calls.csv`, not used to decide. |
| Slide-level class | The class holding the most classified epithelial cells when it reaches 50%; otherwise "mixed", naming every class at 10% or more. |
| Visium spots | A spot holds several cells, often of different types; a Visium class describes a cluster of spots. |

The 50-cell and 50% cut-offs are stated in every run log.
